A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FSFM study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material support reliable comparison, including matching content across relocated appendices and renumbered tables.

before.justification: V1 reports original FSFM evaluations on deepfake detection, face anti-spoofing and diffusion forgery detection, plus ablations and representation analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds within-dataset FF++ results at two compression levels in Table 5.

M1.justification: The CRFR-P masking procedure, MIM and ID architecture, losses, teacher updates and downstream inference remain unchanged. The corrected decoder equation documents the already-described reconstruction operation rather than introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: V3 adds actual training and evaluation on high-compression FF++ c40 alongside c23 in Table 5. This extends coverage to a degraded-input condition within an existing dataset; the other datasets and three principal tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in matched experiments. The new Table 5 reuses existing ViT-B scratch and supervised baselines, MAE, DINO and MCF. CLIP and the specialized comparison methods were already included in v1.

E3.justification: V3 Table 5 adds within-FF++ evaluation, with models separately finetuned and tested on c23 and c40 and assessed using frame-level and video-level AUC. The existing cross-dataset and cross-domain protocols and their stated settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section E.1 adds an analysis of within-dataset performance and robustness under high compression, using separate finetuning at each compression level. Existing masking, decoder, augmentation, loss and scaling ablations, attention analyses and visualizations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean FAS HTER and AUC over five runs. V3 adds no run-count information, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty reporting for the new evaluation.

E6.justification: All numerical results in the nine existing tables are retained. New Table 5 reports FSFM frame/video AUCs of 97.74/99.03 on c23 and 92.08/95.41 on c40. MAE scores 98.64/99.61 and 91.35/94.46, respectively: FSFM trails MAE on c23 but leads all listed baselines on c40. These are newly reported settings, not improvements over v1 results.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the mathematical specification of the decoder output: v1 mistakenly repeats the encoder equation, whereas v3 gives the masked prediction using the decoder. The loss equations otherwise remain unchanged, with no new assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: self-supervised real-face representation learning through the three consistency/coherency/correspondence objectives, transferable vanilla-ViT features, and strong generalization across three face-security tasks.

C2.justification: New Section G identifies demographic bias inherited from pretraining data and missing complementary audio or physiological signals as limitations. Section E.1 interprets the added results as comparable c23 performance and stronger high-compression robustness. Earlier mechanism explanations and computational limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the same preprocessing, architectures, hyperparameters, training budgets and four-RTX-A6000 hardware disclosure. The project-page link is unchanged. Stating that WDF is used 'without processing' restates v1's instruction to use its supplied face images directly.

R1.justification: V3 adds Sun et al.'s 'Towards general visual-linguistic face forgery detection (v2)' to the introduction and bibliography. It also corrects the discussion of temporal representations from intra-frame to inter-frame. Other reference updates mainly concern publication metadata; the overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized language and terminology corrections, adds acknowledgements and two short supplementary sections, and places the supplementary material before the references. It also corrects the online-versus-target description of the existing decoder ablation. Most prose and the scientific narrative are retained.

P2.justification: V3 adds the compact intra-FF++ comparison as Table 5, renumbering v1 Tables 5–9 as Tables 6–10. Existing figures retain their graphic content, while captions, spacing and placement receive limited adjustments as the document is reflowed.

improvement.justification: The added FF++ evaluation provides useful evidence about compression robustness while revealing that FSFM does not lead the c23 comparison. Explicit limitations concerning demographic bias and missing modalities improve qualification of the claims, and the decoder corrections improve technical clarity. These are limited gains: the core method and previously reported results remain unchanged.
